children: India's consumer-price inflation accelerated in August as food and fuel prices continued to rise.

The consumer-price index rose 4.82% from a year earlier, compared with 4.45% in July, government data showed Monday. It was the highest reading this year and since the government revamped the CPI series in January.
The reading came slightly below the 4.9% increase expected by economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.
Food inflation accelerated to 5.95% from 5.52% in July.
Rising food prices and the delayed impact of higher fuel costs have added to inflationary pressures in India, which relies heavily on imported oil and gas.

Inflation is likely to rise further in the coming months as a weak monsoon pushes up food prices, Capital Economics economist Shilan Shah said in a note before the data release. Brent crude's recent rise above $100 a barrel poses an additional risk, Shah said.
Volatile energy prices are also raising business costs that could eventually be passed on to consumers, even though retail fuel prices have been unchanged since May, DBS Group Research said.
With no end in sight to tensions between the U.S. and Iran, investors will continue watching inflation for clues about the Reserve Bank of India's next interest-rate move.
A broader rise in prices is likely to keep inflation above 5% in the second half of the fiscal year, strengthening the case for tighter monetary policy, DBS said.
The central bank held rates steady in August and maintained a neutral stance, citing persistent geopolitical tensions and the need to retain flexibility amid uncertainty.
